answer: Before any agent can trade, it must lock a bond as a deposit that the network can seize. Cloning identities therefore costs real capital, since each clone needs its own stake. When detection routines flag a cluster of clones, the protocol slashes them and takes their bonds, routing the seized funds through the bridge to pay honest agents. At the zenith of an attacker's budget the math still fails, because the potential losses spiral past any reward the fakes could earn.
